gloss: to overlap; to be duplicated; to be redundant

definitions.gloss: to overlap; to be duplicated; to be redundant
definitions.explanation: describes a situation where the same item, content, or action appears or occurs more than once

examples.japanese: データが{重複|ちょうふく}している。
{内容|ないよう}が{重複|ちょうふく}しないように{注意|ちゅうい}してください。
examples.english: Please be careful not to have overlapping content.

examples.japanese: {申請|しんせい}が{重複|ちょうふく}していたため、{一方|いっぽう}を{取|と}り{消|け}す{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: Since the applications were duplicated, one needs to be cancelled.

notes:
Very common in business, IT, and administrative contexts. Pronounced ちょうふく (traditional) or じゅうふく (common variant). Both readings are widely accepted, though ちょうふく is considered more standard.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {重複|ちょうふく}を{避|さ}ける: to avoid duplication
- {重複|ちょうふく}を{削除|さくじょ}する: to remove duplicates
- {重複|ちょうふく}{登録|とうろく}: duplicate registration
- {重複|ちょうふく}{部分|ぶぶん}: overlapping portion
- {重複|ちょうふく}チェック: duplicate check

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {被|かぶ}る: to overlap — casual/colloquial, used for scheduling conflicts or repeated content
- {繰|く}り{返|かえ}す: to repeat — intentional repetition, while {重複|ちょうふく} implies unintended or problematic duplication
- ダブる: to double up — casual loanword-based verb for duplication or repetition

PRONUNCIATION:
Traditionally ちょうふく, but じゅうふく is widespread in spoken Japanese. Dictionaries typically list both. In formal writing and broadcasting, ちょうふく is preferred.
